sections.title: Building Glass Sealant Services in Jakarta
sections.intro: Cracked, brittle, or detached glass joints are the main cause of building glass leaks. We handle sealant work from inspection to complete re-sealing.

items.title: Glass Re-Sealing
items.text: Removing damaged old sealant, cleaning the joints, then applying new sealant so the glass is watertight again.

items.title: Glass Leak Repair
items.text: Tracing leak points on curtain walls, windows, and ACP joints, then repairing the problem areas.

items.title: Curtain Wall & ACP Sealant
items.text: Sealant for glass facades, curtain walls, canopies, and ACP panels on offices, apartments, hotels, and malls.

items.title: Waterproofing Vulnerable Areas
items.text: Extra protection for areas prone to seepage, such as facade corners, window trims, and glass-to-wall joints.

sections.title: Signs Your Glass Sealant Needs Replacing
sections.imageAlt: Sealant being applied to a building glass joint

items.title: Water Seeps In When It Rains
items.text: Water stains, bubbling paint, or wet ceilings around windows mean the glass joints are no longer watertight.

items.title: Cracked, Brittle, or Peeling Sealant
items.text: Jakarta's heat and UV exposure harden and crack sealant over time.

items.title: Condensation or Dust Inside the Glass
items.text: Air and dust getting through gaps show the joints have loosened.

items.title: Wind Noise and Weaker Air Conditioning
items.text: Gaps in the joints let outside air in and increase the load on air conditioning.

items.title: Experience with Jakarta Buildings
items.text: We understand the challenges of buildings in dense urban Jakarta: limited access, building operating hours, and fast-changing weather.

items.title: High-Quality Materials
items.text: We use sealants that withstand heat, high humidity, and pollution, chosen to suit your building's glass and frames.

items.title: Safety Guaranteed

sections.title: Our Glass Sealant Process
sections.imageAlt: Glass facade of a multi-storey building

items.title: Consultation and Site Survey
items.text: We inspect the glass joints and leak points directly at your building, then prepare a work plan.

items.title: Material Selection
items.text: We recommend the sealant type that suits the glass, frames, and Jakarta's weather.

items.title: Removal and Joint Cleaning
items.text: Old sealant is stripped, then the joints are cleaned and dried so the new sealant bonds properly.

items.title: Sealant Application by Rope Access
items.text: Technicians apply new sealant neatly from top to bottom without disrupting building activity.

items.title: Final Inspection and Warranty
items.text: Results are thoroughly inspected, documented, and handed over with a workmanship warranty.

items.q: How long does building glass sealant last?
items.a: It depends on the material and weather exposure. Quality sealant installed correctly usually lasts for years and should be inspected regularly.

items.q: Does sealant work disrupt building activity?
items.a: No. With rope access the work is done from outside the building, scheduled together with building management.

items.q: Is rope access safe for high-rise buildings?
items.a: Yes. Technicians work on twin-rope systems with standard safety equipment and work-at-height procedures in line with OHS regulations.
